title: 1952 AHSME Problem 17
statement: A merchant bought some goods at a discount of \(20\%\) of the list price. He wants to mark them at such a price that he can give a discount of \(20\%\) of the marked price and still make a profit of \(20\%\) of the selling price. The percent of the list price at which he should mark them is:

solutions.text:
Let the list price be \(1.\) The merchant’s cost is \(0.8.\) If the selling price is \(S,\) then \(S-0.8=0.2S,\) so \(S=1.\) If the marked price is \(M,\) the \(20\%\) discount gives \(0.8M=S=1,\) hence \(M=1.25.\)

The marked price must therefore be \(125\%\) of the list price, so the correct answer is C.
hints: Normalize the list price to \(1\) and distinguish cost, marked price, and selling price
A profit equal to \(20\%\) of selling price means the cost is \(80\%\) of selling price
